hints: Focus on what each test is really telling you, one test for a specific methyl group and one test for being easily oxidised.
The yellow precipitate with alkaline iodine is the triiodomethane test, so look for $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ in alcohols or $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ in carbonyls.
Now check which of 1, 2 and 3 can be oxidised by warm dichromate(VI), remembering that ketones resist oxidation while primary alcohols and aldehydes do not.
walkthrough:
**Decode the iodine test**

The yellow precipitate with alkaline aqueous iodine is $\text{CHI}_3$, triiodomethane. This is a positive iodoform test.

It is given by: $$\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}- \text{ group and } \text{CH}_3\text{CO}- \text{ group}$$

**Test structures 1, 2 and 3 for iodoform**

Structure 1 is ethanol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$. It contains $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$, so positive.

Structure 2 is ethanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$. It contains $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$, so positive.

Structure 3 is propanone, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$. It contains $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$, so positive. All three pass the first test.

**Decode the dichromate test**

Warm, acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ is an oxidising agent. A colour change from orange to green means Y has been oxidised.

Primary alcohols are oxidised and aldehydes are oxidised, but ketones are not oxidised.

**Apply to 1, 2 and 3 and conclude**

1, ethanol (primary alcohol), is oxidised to ethanal then ethanoic acid. Colour changes.

2, ethanal (aldehyde), is oxidised to ethanoic acid. Colour changes.

3, propanone (ketone), is not oxidised. No colour change.

So only 1 and 2 satisfy both tests.

options.A: Incorrect. This suggests 1, 2 and 3 are all possible. While all three give the yellow $\text{CHI}_3$ precipitate, 3 (propanone, a ketone) is not oxidised by warm acidified dichromate(VI), so it fails the second test.
options.B: Correct. Both 1 (ethanol) and 2 (ethanal) contain the iodoform group and both are easily oxidised, so both give the yellow precipitate and turn orange dichromate(VI) green.
options.C: Incorrect. This suggests 2 and 3 only. While 2 (ethanal) fits both tests, 3 (propanone) gives the iodoform precipitate but does not react with dichromate(VI) because ketones resist oxidation.
options.D: Incorrect. This suggests 1 only. Compound 1 (ethanol) does fit both tests, but it misses that 2 (ethanal) also fits both tests, as aldehydes give a positive iodoform test and are oxidised by dichromate(VI).
